title: Enhancing 3-D Random Walk Capacitance Solver with Analytic Surface Green's Functions of Transition Cubes
problem: Floating random walk (FRW) based capacitance extraction loses accuracy under advanced process technologies with complex stratified dielectric profiles, as it pre-computes surface Green's functions for only a finite set of transition cubes and makes approximations during simulation. Traditional approaches cannot accurately handle arbitrary stratified dielectrics in realistic transition regions.
motivation: Accurate capacitance extraction is critical for circuit design verification and layout optimization in advanced semiconductor manufacturing nodes.
method: The paper derives analytic surface Green's functions (AGF) for transition cubes with arbitrary stratified dielectrics and develops a fast algorithm to compute them efficiently. These analytic functions are integrated into the floating random walk process to create FRW-AGF, which directly models realistic transition cubes without pre-computed approximations while maintaining parallel scalability.
key_novelty: Analytic derivation of surface Green's functions for transition cubes with arbitrary stratified dielectrics, eliminating approximation errors inherent in discrete pre-computed tables.
contributions: Analytic surface Green's function formulation for stratified dielectric transition cubes
Fast AGF algorithm achieving 100x speedup over state-of-the-art methods
FRW-AGF solver incorporating analytic Green's functions into floating random walk for improved accuracy
Reduction of capacitance extraction errors below 5% without performance or scalability degradation

metrics.accuracy: All errors <5% to golden values vs RWCap4

primary_theme: Analytic Green's functions for accurate capacitance extraction
